topic: The samurai who broke the dam
title_jp: {隼人|はやと}さまの{伝説|でんせつ|legend|3}
context: Monday afternoon, a quiet day as the harvest ends: アルちゃん walked up to the small museum at {鷹ノ原城跡|たかのはらじょうあと} and photographed a painting of a samurai. On the {縁側|えんがわ}, ハナおばあちゃん tells him the legend of {黒鉄隼人|くろがねはやと}, who broke his lord's dam to save the village.
scene: You photographed a samurai painting at the castle-ruins museum. On the {縁側|えんがわ}, ハナおばあちゃん tells you who he was.

phrases.jp: {侍|さむらい|samurai|3}がみんなお{金持ち|かねもち}だったわけではないんですね。
phrases.en: So not all samurai were rich.
phrases.note: みんな〜わけではない = not all of them. Many low-ranking samurai were in fact quite poor.

phrases.jp: えっ、{まさか||no way, surely not|4}！{本当|ほんとう}ですか。
phrases.note: まさか reacts to something you didn't expect at all. Casual: え、マジ？

phrases.jp: へえ、そうなんだ。{全然|ぜんぜん}{知らなかった|しらなかった}。
phrases.en: Huh, is that so. I had no idea.
phrases.note: へえ with a rising tone shows real interest. A flat へえ sounds bored.

phrases.jp: それは{気の毒|きのどく|pitiful, a shame|3}ですね。
phrases.note: Sympathy for someone else's bad luck. Not for your own: then say {残念|ざんねん}.

phrases.jp: だから{今|いま}でも{鷹祭り|たかまつり|the town's hawk festival|2}で{感謝|かんしゃ|gratitude|3}するんですね。
phrases.en: So that's why people still thank him at the {鷹祭り|たかまつり}.
phrases.note: だから〜んですね: the 'ah, now I get it' reaction that links what you just heard to what you knew.

dialogue_setting: The {縁側|えんがわ} of the {田中|たなか} house, Monday afternoon. ハナおばあちゃん has come over with persimmons; アルちゃん shows her a photo on his phone.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: おばあちゃん、{城跡|しろあと|castle ruins|2}の{博物館|はくぶつかん|museum|3}で、この{侍|さむらい|samurai|3}の{絵|え}を{見ました|みました}。
dialogue.en: おばあちゃん, I saw this painting of a samurai at the museum by the castle ruins.

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: ああ、{隼人|はやと}さまじゃ。{大雨|おおあめ}で{村|むら}が{危険|きけん|danger, dangerous|3}になった{時|とき}、{殿様|とのさま|feudal lord|2}の{許し|ゆるし|permission|3}なしでダムを{壊して|こわして|to break, destroy|4}、{村|むら}を{守った|まもった|to protect|4}んじゃ。
dialogue.en: Ah, that's {隼人|はやと}さま. When heavy rain put the village in danger, he broke the lord's dam without permission and saved the village.
dialogue.note: じゃ is old-fashioned/regional for だ: {隼人|はやと}さまだ, {守|まも}ったんだ.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: えっ、すごい！でも、それって{殿様|とのさま|feudal lord|2}に{逆らった|さからった|to go against, defy|3}ってことですよね？
dialogue.en: Wow, amazing! But that means he defied his lord, right?

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: そうじゃ。でも{殿様|とのさま|feudal lord|2}が{嫌い|きらい}だったわけではないんじゃよ。{村|むら}の{人|ひと}を{見捨てられなかった|みすてられなかった|to abandon|3}んじゃ。
dialogue.en: That's right. But it's not that he disliked his lord. He just couldn't abandon the village people.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: なるほど…。{悪い|わるい}{人|ひと}だったわけじゃないんですね。それで、どうなったんですか。
dialogue.en: I see… So he wasn't a bad man. And then what happened to him?

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {罰|ばつ|punishment|3}として、お{米|こめ}の{給料|きゅうりょう|salary, pay|4}を{半分|はんぶん}にされたんじゃ。でも{村|むら}の{人|ひと}は{今|いま}でも{感謝|かんしゃ|gratitude|3}{しとる||(dialect) = している|1}よ。
dialogue.en: As punishment, his rice pay was cut in half. But the people here are still grateful to him today.
dialogue.note: しとる = している (western/rural Japan). Samurai were paid in rice, not coins.

listening.intro: That evening your phone buzzes while you're washing up: a voicemail from {田中|たなか}さん.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{田中|たなか}だ。{今夜|こんや}は{町|まち}の{寄り合い|よりあい|neighbourhood meeting|2}で{遅く|おそく}なる。
lines.en: アルちゃん, it's {田中|たなか}. I'll be late tonight because of the town meeting.

lines.jp: {晩飯|ばんめし|dinner (casual)|3}は{先に|さきに}{食べとって|たべとって|(dialect) = 食べていて|2}くれ。8{時|じ}ごろには{帰る|かえる}{ずら||(Nagano dialect) = だろう|1}。
lines.en: Go ahead and eat dinner without me. I'll probably be back around eight.

listening.question: {田中|たなか}さんは{何時|なんじ}ごろ{帰ります|かえります}か。
listening.explain: 8{時|じ}ごろには{帰|かえ}るずら = he'll probably be home around eight, after dinner, which he says to eat without him.

grammar.form: verb / い-adj: plain + わけではない ({行|い}くわけではない, {高|たか}いわけではない) · な-adj / noun: + な + わけではない ({嫌|きら}いなわけではない) · past: plain past + わけではない ({嫌|きら}いだったわけではない, {悪|わる}い{人|ひと}だったわけではない) · casual: わけじゃない
grammar.explanation: Corrects a conclusion someone might draw: 'it's not that…'. With みんな or {全部|ぜんぶ} it means 'not all'. In speech it's わけじゃない. Don't confuse it with わけがない ('there's no way'), a strong denial.
mark: 嫌いだったわけではない
悪い人だったわけじゃない
金持ちだったわけではない
怒ってるわけじゃない

examples.jp: {日本人|にほんじん}がみんな{寿司|すし}が{好き|すき}なわけではない。
examples.en: Not every Japanese person likes sushi.

examples.jp: {怒って|おこって}るわけじゃないよ。ちょっと{疲れて|つかれて}るだけ。
examples.en: I'm not angry. I'm just a bit tired.

quiz.question: {肉|にく}が{嫌い|きらい}＿＿わけではないけど、{今日|きょう}は{魚|さかな}がいい。
quiz.en: It's not that I dislike meat, but today I'd like fish.
quiz.explain: A な-adjective in the present takes な before わけ: {嫌|きら}いなわけではない.

quiz_more.question: {侍|さむらい|samurai|3}がみんなお{金持ち|かねもち}＿＿。
quiz_more.explain: 'Not all' = みんな〜わけではない. わけがない would mean 'there's no way they were rich'.

quiz_more.question: {怒って|おこって}る＿＿よ。{眠い|ねむい}だけ。
quiz_more.en: It's not that I'm angry. I'm just sleepy.
quiz_more.explain: Correcting what the other person thinks, casually: わけじゃない. The others deny or conclude too strongly.

kanji.meaning: castle ruins, site of a castle
kanji.where: On the stone marker at the top of the hill and on the town signposts: {鷹ノ原城跡|たかのはらじょうあと} →.
kanji.related: In names it's often read じょうせき or じょうあと, as in {鷹ノ原城跡|たかのはらじょうあと}.
kanji.breakdown: {城跡|しろあと}: 城 castle + 跡 trace, remains → 'what's left of a castle'.

tip.title: Why so many towns have only stone walls
tip.body: After the Meiji government's 1873 castle order ({廃城令|はいじょうれい}), most castles were torn down or sold, so many towns have only a {城跡|しろあと}. Only twelve original keeps ({天守|てんしゅ}) survive today. One is in nearby {松本|まつもと}: worth a day trip.

challenge.prompt: At dinner {恵子|けいこ}さん laughs: 「ハナさんの{話|はなし}、{長かった|ながかった}でしょう？アルちゃん、{歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}なの？」 Say it's not that you love history, but ハナおばあちゃん's stories are interesting.

options.jp: {歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}なわけじゃないんですけど、ハナおばあちゃんの{話|はなし}は{面白い|おもしろい}んです。
options.why: な-adjective + な + わけじゃない, soft polite style for your host mum.

options.jp: {歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}だわけじゃないんですけど、ハナおばあちゃんの{話|はなし}は{面白い|おもしろい}んです。
options.why: Wrong form: a present な-adjective needs な before わけ, not だ.

options.jp: {歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}なわけがないんですけど、ハナおばあちゃんの{話|はなし}は{面白い|おもしろい}んです。
options.why: わけがない = 'there's no way I love history': far too strong and odd here.

options.jp: {歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}なわけじゃねえけど、ハナおばあちゃんの{話|はなし}は{面白い|おもしろい}よ。
options.why: じゃねえ is rough male slang: too rude for talking to {恵子|けいこ}さん.

challenge.model_answer: {歴史|れきし}が{大好き|だいすき}なわけじゃないんですけど、ハナおばあちゃんの{話|はなし}は{面白い|おもしろい}んです。
challenge.hint: な-adjective + な + わけじゃない, polite but soft
challenge.explanation: {大好|だいす}きなわけじゃない corrects her guess without saying 'no' flatly: な-adjectives take な before わけ. 〜んですけど softens it, and 〜んです explains your feeling politely, right for your host mum.

vocab.note: Also {武士|ぶし}, the more formal, historical word.
Written version of {危|あぶ}ない; on signs: {危険|きけん}! Keep out.
How villagers spoke of their lord. Today also jokes about a bossy man: {殿様|とのさま}みたい.
Also {約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}る = keep a promise, ルールを{守|まも}る = follow rules.
Takes に: {親|おや}に{逆|さか}らう = to disobey your parents.
{罰|ばつ}ゲーム = forfeit in a party game. 〜として = as.
{給料日|きゅうりょうび} = payday, the happiest day of the month.
Deeper than ありがとう: 〜に{感謝|かんしゃ}する. Common in speeches and letters.
Literally 'poison to the spirit'. For other people's misfortune only.
Alone as a reaction, or まさか〜とは{思|おも}わなかった = never imagined.

kanji_study.parts: ⻌ road/movement radical + 屰, a person drawn upside down → walking the road the wrong way round: reverse, go against.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 送 (send) or 迷 (lost): all have ⻌, but only 逆 has the upside-down figure 屰.

kanji_study.parts: 阝 hill radical (on the left) + 㑒 'gathered together', which gives the sound ケン → hills crowded together: steep, risky ground.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 検 (inspect, 木 on the left) or 験 (test, 馬 on the left): 険 has the hill radical 阝.

extras.title: Reacting while someone tells a story
extras.title_jp: {話|はなし}を{聞く|きく}ときのあいづち
extras.intro: Japanese listeners react all the time; silence sounds like you're not listening.

items.note: Rising tone = interested. The all-purpose reaction.
Casual surprise, not an accusation of lying.
Asks the speaker to go on. Polite: それで、どうなったんですか。
Avoid it with teachers or bosses: it can sound like you're judging. Use そうなんですね.
When the story is unfair to someone.

extras.title: Samurai-drama speech (recognise, don't use)
extras.title_jp: {時代劇|じだいげき|period drama|2}の{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: You'll hear these in period dramas and in {隼人|はやと}'s legends. In real life they only get laughs.

items.note: Drama speech only. Modern: {私|わたし}, {僕|ぼく}.
Drama speech only. {拙者|せっしゃ}は{侍|さむらい}でござる = I am a samurai.
Drama speech only. Grateful and a bit embarrassed.

items.jp: {知らぬ|しらぬ|(archaic) = 知らない|1}
items.note: 〜ぬ = 〜ない in old speech. Still in set phrases: {知|し}らぬ{間|ま}に.
